verdicts.why: The brief explicitly states the operator runs four delivery vans.
The brief states maintenance records live in a glovebox folder per van, meaning a physical folder in each van.
The persona answer confirms one van missed its brake service under the current system, establishing that services are being missed.
This is a hypothesis not asserted by the persona; the brief states the goal but does not confirm centralisation will definitively prevent missed services.
The persona answers never specify which types of maintenance records need tracking; this is presented as an unknown but the examples given (oil changes, tyre rotations, MOT) are not from the brief.
The workflow answer clearly identifies who logs what — drivers log issues/mileage and the operator enters completed work — so this is not an unknown; it is a grounded fact misclassified as unknown.
The persona answers do not describe any mechanism for surfacing upcoming services beyond the operator checking weekly; alerting methods are not mentioned anywhere in the brief.
The brief and persona answers make no mention of migrating historical glovebox records, so this deferral is not supported or contradicted — it is an invented framing of an issue never raised.
The success criterion explicitly states no overdue services across the fleet for a full quarter, matching this statement closely.
The persona's success answer explicitly states the full history of any van must be printable when sold.
The brief mentions selling a van as a success criterion but does not indicate it is anticipated as a near-term event rather than a future possibility.
The workflow answer states drivers log an issue or mileage when they park up, directly supporting this statement.
The workflow answer states the operator checks upcoming services weekly and books the garage.
The workflow answer states completed work gets entered from the invoice, directly matching this statement.
The three steps and roles described map directly to the workflow answer: driver logging at park-up, operator weekly review and booking, and operator post-service entry from invoice.

payload.why: The trigger logic for service due dates is the mechanical heart of the system and not addressed in the brief, making this a high-value question; it loses one point because the problem, users, and workflow are also still completely uncharted and this single question leaves those equally critical gaps unexplored.

The SPEC is sufficient for a first vertical slice — roles, workflow steps, success criteria, and the four-van scope are all represented — but it is padded with redundant concern-coverage entries that repeat facts already stated in the Facts/Decisions sections, and it carries several open-ended gaps (service interval trigger type, whether historical glovebox records are to be migrated) that were surfaced in the consultation but left unresolved rather than explicitly scoped out.
